key_insight: Symmetry-guided optimization uses Hilbert–Schmidt asymmetry to steer variational quantum states toward a target symmetry sector without requiring symmetry-preserving circuits.
engineering_relevance: This approach can improve the reliability of variational quantum eigensolvers while retaining flexibility in state-preparation circuit design.
method: Quantify deviation from a specified symmetry using quantum-accessible Hilbert–Schmidt asymmetry.
Use asymmetry to guide optimization toward the target sector alongside the energy objective.
Test singlet-state targeting under collective SU(2) symmetry.
evidence_signal: Proof-of-principle tests on a five-qubit nuclear two-cluster Hamiltonian and collective spin models with up to 12 particles increased singlet probability and improved energy accuracy and ground-state fidelity compared with direct energy minimization.
watch_item: Performance beyond these benchmarks, including the measurement cost and noise sensitivity of asymmetry estimation, remains to be established.
paper_title: Symmetry-guided algorithms for variational quantum optimization
